evidence: Reviewed only the supplied exact-proposal packet, validator schema, and pinned primary source https://arxiv.org/html/2605.07006v1. Primary-source check: Definition 1.12 defines beta-smoothness by C1 regularity, beta>=0, and the displayed global quadratic upper model; Section 3 explicitly assumes C2 regularity throughout. Section 2 states the attained-minimum convention for the notes. Theorem 3.7 has the proposed best-iterate gradient norm and constant 2, while its printed line omits positive h and nonempty N. Thus retaining Euclidean C2 and attainment is faithful to the source context, although neither is a logically minimal hypothesis of the algebraic descent implication. Exact-proposal assessment: accepted as an explicit ordinary-real-domain overlay, not an amended quotation of the pinned source. For beta>0, h<=1/beta and beta*h<=1 are equivalent. Positive h and positive natural N make the averaging and square root defined with a nonnegative radicand. The C2 upper-model premise is exactly source beta-smoothness in the section context; no convexity, PL, gradient-Lipschitz premise, uniqueness, or coercivity is inserted. Independent sufficiency calculation: setting g_k=grad f(x_k), the actual update and upper model give f(x_(k+1))<=f(x_k)-h*(1-beta*h/2)*||g_k||^2<=f(x_k)-(h/2)*||g_k||^2. Summing and using f(x_N)>=f(z) gives (h/2)*sum ||g_k||^2<=f(x_0)-f(z). A nonempty finite family has a squared norm at most its average; positive division and the monotone nonnegative square root give the exact proposed conclusion. All four witnesses were checked independently. For f(t)=t^2/2 on R, beta=1, z=0 and x_0=1, f is C2, z is a global minimizer, and its upper model holds with equality. With h=0,N=1 the update is x_(k+1)=x_k, the left side is 1, and the ordinary denominator is zero; totalized division would give RHS 0. With h=-1,N=1 the update is x_(k+1)=2*x_k, the left side is 1 and the radicand is -1; ordinary real sqrt is undefined, while Lean Real.sqrt is zero. With h=1,N=0 the update sends every iterate after x_0 to zero, but the indexed family is empty and no real finite minimum or witness exists. For f(t)=0 on R, beta=0,z=0,x_0=1,h=1,N=1 the C2 upper model, attainment and constant update hold, and the algebraic bound is 0<=0; only the printed ordinary reciprocal 1/beta is undefined. These are domain witnesses; the zero-beta case is not a counterexample to the algebraic theorem. Minimality distinction: beta>0 is needed here only to retain the ordinary reciprocal wording within beta>=0, not to ensure convergence of every algebraic extension; h>0 and N>=1 repair existing normalized expressions. The beta=0 algebraic endpoint, arbitrary real beta, complete-Hilbert ambient space, and totalized-gradient/no-separate-regularity Lean implication remain separately labeled extensions. This acceptance neither identifies those extensions with the source nor certifies compilation from a hash.
